## Structure and components

- [passage] If using [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) with [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort), be sure to include at least one field in your sort that contains unique values, before passing results to [`skip()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#using-skip-with-sort · keywords: cursor, pagination, skip(), sort() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.limit.md
- [passage] - Only contain one second of temporal resolution, so [ObjectId](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-objectid) values created within the same second do not have a guaranteed ordering, and — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#descending-order · keywords: pagination
- [passage] The second case occurs when the merge part of the split pipeline contains a stage which may write temporary data to disk, such as $group, and the client has specified allowDiskUse:true. In this case, assuming that there are no other stages in the merge pipeline which require the primary shard, the merge runs on a randomly-selected shard in the set of shards targeted by the aggregation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: blocking sort · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [passage] be sure to include at least one field in your sort that contains unique values, before passing results to the [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#using-skip-with-sorted-results · keywords: pagination, $skip · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md
- [passage] When a [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) immediately follows another [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip), the two stages can coalesce into a single [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) where the skip amount is the *sum* of the two initial skip amounts. For example, a pipeline contains the following sequence: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#skip-skip-coalescence · keywords: pagination, $skip

## How it works

- [passage] A query that exceeds either 100 megabytes or the available memory spills to disk. It writes intermediate data to storage to save memory, which can cause lowered performance. Use the [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) parameter or [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) method to configure this behavior. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#query-spill · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, allowDiskUseByDefault, cursor.allowDiskUse()
- [fact] Offset pagination is inconsistent under concurrent writes: inserts or deletes between requests cause duplicate or missing items. Keyset is more stable for changes before the current page but not immune; mutable sort fields can still cause duplicates or misses. — https://begriffs.com/posts/2016-03-30-five-ways-to-paginate.html · keywords: pagination, query operator anti-pattern, Pagination Patterns (skip-limit vs range-keyset)
- [passage] When you sort based on an array field that is indexed with a multikey index, the query plan includes an in-memory sort stage unless both of the following are true: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: blocking sort, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/
- [passage] When you sort based on an array field that is indexed with a [multikey index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multikey), the query plan includes an [in-memory sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-in-memory-sort) stage unless both of the following are true: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#sorting · keywords: blocking sort, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md
- [passage] Returning paginated results in ascending order is similar to the previous, but uses [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt) with an *ascending* sort order: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#ascending-order · keywords: pagination, $gt
- [fact] When combining skip() with sort(), include a field with unique values (easiest: _id) in the sort. Duplicate sort values can yield inconsistent order across executions, especially while the collection receives writes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.2/reference/method/cursor.skip/ · keywords: pagination, Pagination Patterns (skip-limit vs range-keyset)
- [passage] Examples of stages that can write temporary files to disk when [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#std-label-aggregate-cmd-allowDiskUse) is `true` are: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#memory-restrictions · keywords: blocking sort, true · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] - Using `{ allowDiskUse: true }` to allow writing temporary files out to disk when `allowDiskUseByDefault` is set to `false` — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: blocking sort, { allowDiskUse: true }, allowDiskUseByDefault, false · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sortByCount.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md
- [passage] - Using `{ allowDiskUse: false }` to prohibit writing temporary files out to disk when `allowDiskUseByDefault` is set to `true` — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: blocking sort, { allowDiskUse: false }, allowDiskUseByDefault, true · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sortByCount.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md
- [passage] Then the second [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) stage can coalesce into the first [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) stage and result in a single [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) stage where the skip amount `7` is the sum of the two initial limits `5` and `2`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#skip-skip-coalescence · keywords: pagination, $skip,  is the sum of the two initial limits ,  and 

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To check if MongoDB must perform an in-memory sort, append [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) to the query and check the [explain results](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results). If the query plan contains a `SORT` stage, then MongoDB must perform an in-memory sort operation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#sort-and-index-use · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, index, cursor.explain(), SORT · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse.md
- [passage] To avoid an in-memory sort, place the range filter after the sort predicate. For more information on in-memory sorts, see cursor.allowDiskUse(). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: blocking sort, cursor · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/
- [passage] To avoid an in-memory sort, place the range filter after the sort predicate. For more information on in-memory sorts, see [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md#range · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, cursor.allowDiskUse()
- [fact] Check for a blocking sort with explain(): a SORT stage in the plan means a blocking sort; no SORT stage means the index supplies the order. Use hint() when testing candidate indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/ · keywords: blocking sort, index, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [passage] To see full aggregation examples that use the [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) stage, see the [Complete Aggregation Pipeline Tutorials.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/aggregation-complete-examples.md#std-label-aggregation-complete-examples) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#learn-more · keywords: pagination, $skip

## Measurements and reference values

- [fact] allowDiskUse has no effect on sorts answered by an index, or on blocking sorts that fit under 100 MB. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/ · keywords: blocking sort, index, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [statement] Tencent Cloud reports that placing a range field ahead of the sort field forced an in-memory sort, and that reordering to ESR cut an order query from second-level latency to about 10 ms and a report from timeout to 200 ms. These are single-vendor anecdotes, not benchmarks. — https://intl.cloud.tencent.com/document/product/240/80772 · keywords: blocking sort, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [passage] | **Instance RAM** | **Comparable Tier** | **maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes Default** | | --- | --- | --- | | 256GB+ | M200+ | 2048 MB | | 128GB - 256GB | M80-M140 | 1024 MB | | 32GB - 128GB | M50-M60 | 512 MB | | 16GB | M40 | 400 MB | | 8GB | M30 | 250 MB | | 2GB - 4GB | M10-M20 | 100 MB | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: blocking sort

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] | **MongoDB Version** | **Changes** | | --- | --- | | 6.1 | Slow operation log messages include [cache refresh time fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-cache-refresh-times) | | 6.2 | Slow operation log messages include a `queryFramework` field that indicates which query engine executed the query: `queryFramework: "classic"` indicates that the classic engine executed the query.; `queryFramework: "sbe"` indicates that the slot-based query execution engine executed the query. | | 6.3 | Slow operation log messages and [database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) entries include a `cpuNanos` field that specifies the total CPU time spent by a query operation in nanoseconds. The `cpuNanos` field is only available on Linux systems. | | 7.0 (and 6.0.13, 5.0.24) | The `totalOplogSlotDurationMicros` in the slow query log message shows the time between a write operation getting a commit timestamp to commit the storage engine writes and actually committing. `mongod` supports parallel writes. However, it commits write operations with commit timestamps in any order. For example, consider the following writes with commit timestamps: writeA with Timestamp1; writeB with Timestamp2; writeC with Timestamp3 Suppose writeB commits first at Timestamp2. Replication is paused until writeA commits because writeA's oplog entry with Timestamp1 is required for replication to copy the oplog to secondary replica set members. | | 8.0 | The slow query output includes a `queues` document that contains information about the operation's [queues](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#std-label-server-status-queues). Each queue in the `queues` field contains a `totalTimeQueuedMicros` field that contains the total cumulative time in microseconds that the operation spent in the corresponding queue. The `queryShapeHash` field for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) is also included in the slow query log when available. If a command with a specific query shape is [rejected](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/operation-rejection-filters.md#std-label-operation-rejection-filters), MongoDB logs a message that states the query command was rejected. The message contains the query namespace, `queryShapeHash`, and the command with the rejected query. MongoDB only logs the message if the log verbosity level is set to at least `2`. | | 8.1 | Slow query log messages contain new metrics if the query execution writes temporary files to disk. These metrics are prefixed by the query execution stage that caused the query to exceed the memory limit. For example, `sortSpills` indicates the number of times that the sort stage of query execution wrote temporary files to disk. `<executionPart>Spills` indicates the number of times the corresponding query execution stage wrote temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledBytes` indicates the size, in bytes, of the memory released by writing temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledDataStorageSize` indicates the size, in bytes, of disk space used for temporary files.; `<executionPart>SpilledRecords` indicates the number of records written to temporary files on disk. For more information on writing temporary files to disk, see [`allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) | | 8.3 | Slow query log entries have an optional `originalQueryShapeHash` field that contains that query shape of the following operations that originate on the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#std-program-mongos) : [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find); [`aggregate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.aggregate); [`count`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.count); [`distinct`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.distinct) The original query shape of the `mongos` operation may differ after the `mongos` sends the operation to the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-program-mongod) . MongoDB 8.3 also introduces slow in-progress query log entries. Queries trigger a slow-in progress log during execution. These logs contain less information than standard slow query logs. MongoDB logs queries at most once if the query's duration surpasses the [`operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs) When an operation specifies a [time limit for a query](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents/specify-query-timeout.md#std-label-manual-query-timeout), slow query logs contain a `deadline` field. `deadline` indicates the time the operation must complete by, which is equal to the time at the start of the operation plus the value of the query timeout. | | 9.0 | When a query shape has query knobs set through [`setQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) or [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), slow query log entries include a `queryKnobs` document. The document shows the effective value of each knob and where the value comes from, with the same shape as the [explain output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-output-query-knobs). For details, see [Query Knobs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-query-knobs) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#version-specific-changes · keywords: blocking sort, count, cursor, index, query shape, sharded query targeting
- [fact] Sort and limit behave differently in the router. Unsorted results come from a round-robin over shard cursors. With limit(), mongos passes the limit to each shard and re-applies it to the merged result. With skip(), mongos cannot push the skip down: it passes limit+skip to the shards, then skips while assembling results. Deep skip on a sharded collection therefore costs more. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, pagination, sharded query targeting, Sharded Query Targeting and Scatter-Gather
- [fact] ESR classification: $ne, $nin and $regex are range operators, not equality. $in alone is equality. With a sort, $in under 201 elements expands and merges via a SORT_MERGE stage (acts like equality); at 201 or more it behaves like a range and later index keys cannot supply the sort. The 201 threshold is documented as not guaranteed across versions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/ · keywords: $in, blocking sort, index, query operator anti-pattern, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [passage] You can't configure the threshold that [`$sample`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sample) uses to determine when to scan the entire collection. The threshold is 5%. If the size is greater than 5% of the total number of documents in the collection, [`$sample`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sample) performs a [top-k](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-limit-results) sort by a generated random value. The top-k sort could spill to disk if the sample documents are larger than 100MB. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md#pseudo-random-cursor-behavior · keywords: blocking sort, count, cursor, $sample
- [fact] Keyset pagination cannot jump to an arbitrary page, since reaching page N generally means visiting earlier pages, and it does not easily return total counts. It suits infinite scroll and next/previous navigation. Skip-limit suits shallow paging, small datasets and jump-to-page UIs. — https://blog.openreplay.com/pagination-patterns-mongodb/ · keywords: count, pagination, query operator anti-pattern, Pagination Patterns (skip-limit vs range-keyset)

- [passage] If MongoDB cannot obtain the sort order with an index scan, then MongoDB uses a top-k sort algorithm. This algorithm buffers the first `k` results (or last, depending on the sort order) seen so far by the underlying index or collection access. If the memory footprint of these `k` results exceeds 100 megabytes, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) with a value of `false` (in which case, the query fails). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#limit-results · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, index, cursor.allowDiskUse(), false
- [passage] Since reading.timestamp is not included in an index, MongoDB must perform an in-memory sort operation to return results in the requested sort order. By specifying cursor.allowDiskUse(false), MongoDB cannot process the sort operation if it requires more than 100 megabytes of system memory. If the operation requires more than 100 megabytes of system memory, MongoDB would return an error. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/ · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse.md
- [fact] ESR guideline: $in used alone is an equality operator (a series of equality matches). With .sort(), an $in of fewer than 201 elements is expanded and merged in index sort order by a SORT_MERGE stage, behaving like equality; with 201 or more elements it is ordered like a range, subsequent index fields cannot be used for sorting, and it behaves like a range predicate. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/ · keywords: $in, blocking sort, index, $in and $or Index Bounds and Union Plans

- [passage] When a [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort) precedes a [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit) and there are no intervening stages that modify the number of documents, the optimizer can coalesce the [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit) into the [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort). - [passage] Some stages can't output any documents until they have processed all incoming documents. These pipeline stages must keep their stage output in RAM until all incoming documents are processed. As a result, these pipeline stages may require more space than the 100 MB limit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#memory-restrictions · keywords: blocking sort · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] For memory-intensive expressions that the per-operation limit does not cover, MongoDB applies a limit on the maximum memory that a subset of expressions can use. The default of this limit is 100 megabytes. To change this limit, set the [`internalQueryMaxSingleExpressionMemoryUsageBytes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.internalQueryMaxSingleExpressionMemoryUsageBytes) parameter at startup or at runtime. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#per-operation-memory-limit · keywords: blocking sort, internalQueryMaxSingleExpressionMemoryUsageBytes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] As each stage in a `$facet` executes, the resulting document is limited to 100 megabytes. Note the [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#std-label-aggregate-cmd-allowDiskUse) flag doesn't affect the 100 megabyte size limit, since `$facet` can't spill to disk. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet.md#considerations · keywords: blocking sort, $facet
- [passage] The view's underlying aggregation pipeline is subject to the 100 megabyte memory limit for blocking sort and blocking group operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#view-pipelines · keywords: blocking sort
- [passage] The [`$bucket`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucket.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-bucket) stage has a limit of 100 megabytes of RAM. By default, if the stage exceeds this limit, [`$bucket`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucket.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-bucket) returns an error. To allow more space for stage processing, use the [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#std-label-aggregate-cmd-allowDiskUse) option to enable aggregation pipeline stages to write data to temporary files. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucket.md#bucket-and-memory-restrictions · keywords: blocking sort, $bucket
- [passage] Sort stages, counted separately by sort type and by whether the sort has a limit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: blocking sort
- [passage] The [`$bucketAuto`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucketauto.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-bucketAuto) stage has a limit of 100 megabytes of RAM. By default, if the stage exceeds this limit, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk. For details, see [`allowDiskUseByDefault`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucketAuto.md#bucketauto-and-memory-restrictions · keywords: blocking sort, $bucketAuto, allowDiskUseByDefault
- [passage] - A single [`$accumulator`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md#mongodb-group-grp.-accumulator) operation exceeds its specified memory limit. If you specify the [`allowDiskUse`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.aggregate) option, the operator stores the in-progress operation on disk and finishes the operation in memory. Once the operation finishes, the results from disk and memory are merged together using the [merge](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md#std-label-accumulator-merge) function. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md#merge-two-states-with-merge · keywords: blocking sort, $accumulator, allowDiskUse
- [passage] Slow query log messages contain new metrics if the query execution writes temporary files to disk. These metrics are prefixed by the query execution stage that caused the query to exceed the memory limit. For example, sortSpills indicates the number of times that the sort stage of query execution wrote temporary files to disk. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: blocking sort
- [passage] MongoDB writes this log message only when an operation exceeds the per-operation memory limit and cannot spill to disk. If a stage that can spill to disk exceeds the limit and allowDiskUse is false, MongoDB ends the operation with the QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed error and does not write this log message. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: blocking sort · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md
- [passage] To learn more about related pipeline stages, see the [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit) guide. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.md#learn-more · keywords: pagination, $limit
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.0, the [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) pipeline aggregation has a 64-bit integer limit. Values passed to the pipeline which exceed this limit will return a invalid argument error. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#definition · keywords: pagination, $skip · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md
- [passage] If the results of one of your [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort) pipeline stages exceed the limit, consider [adding a $limit stage.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#std-label-sort-limit-sequence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#memory-restrictions · keywords: pagination, $sort · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] - Add a [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit) stage after a [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort) stage so that the sort keeps only the documents you need. To learn more, see [$sort and $limit Memory Optimization.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#std-label-sort-limit-sequence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#per-operation-memory-limit · keywords: pagination, $limit, $sort · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) corresponds to the `LIMIT ...` clause in a SQL (Structured Query Language) `SELECT` statement. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/query/limit.md#how-does-the-compass-query-compare-to-mongodb-and-sql-queries · keywords: pagination, $skip, LIMIT ..., SELECT · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/query/limit.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/query/skip.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/query/skip.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `find` | string | The name of the collection or [view](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#std-label-views-landing-page) to query. | | `filter` | document | Optional. The query predicate. If unspecified, all documents in the collection match the predicate. | | [sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-sort) | document | Optional. The sort specification for the ordering of the results. | | `projection` | document | Optional. The [projection specification](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/project-fields-from-query-results.md#std-label-projections) to determine which fields to include in the returned documents. [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operations on views do not support the following [find command projection operators:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/projection.md#std-label-projection-operators-ref) [`$`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-); [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch); [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/slice.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-slice); [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) | | `hint` | string or document | Optional. Index specification. Specify either the index name as a string or the index key pattern. If specified, the query system only considers plans using the hinted index. With the following exception, `hint` is required if the command includes the `min` or `max` fields. `hint` is not required with `min` or `max` if the `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `skip` | positive integer | Optional. Number of documents to skip. Defaults to 0. | | `limit` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents to return. If unspecified, then defaults to no limit. A limit of 0 is equivalent to setting no limit. | | `batchSize` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents that can be returned in each batch of a query result. By default, the `find` command has an initial `batchSize` of the lesser of `101` documents or 16 mebibytes (MiB) worth of documents. Subsequent batches have a maximum size of 16 MiB. This option can enforce a smaller limit than 16 MiB, but not a larger one. When set, the `batchSize` is the lesser of `batchSize` documents or 16 MiB worth of documents. A `batchSize` of `0` means that the cursor is established, but no documents are returned in the first batch. Unlike the previous wire protocol version, a batchSize of 1 for the [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) command does not close the cursor. To specify batch size for subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) operations, use [`batchSize()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.batchsize.md#mongodb-method-cursor.batchSize) in mongosh. | | `singleBatch` | boolean | Optional. Determines whether to close the cursor after the first batch. Defaults to false. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). Any comment set on a `find` command is inherited by any subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands run on the `find` cursor. | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. If you do not specify a value for `maxTimeMS`, operations will not time out. A value of `0` explicitly specifies the default unbounded behavior. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) When specifying [`linearizable read concern`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-), always use `maxTimeMS` in case a majority of data bearing members are unavailable. `maxTimeMS` ensures that the operation does not block indefinitely and instead returns an error if the read concern cannot be fulfilled. [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) is unrelated to [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout). [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) limits processing time, while [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout) prevents idle-time expiration. A cursor's idle time does not contribute to its processing time. | | `readConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [read concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-read-concern) The `readConcern` option has the following syntax: `readConcern: { level: <value> }` Possible read concern levels are: [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-). This is the default read concern level for read operations against the primary and secondaries.; [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-). Available for read operations against the primary and secondaries. [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-) behaves the same as [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-) against the primary and non-sharded secondaries. The query returns the instance's most recent data.; [`"majority"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-majority-). Available for replica sets that use [WiredTiger storage engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger); [`"linearizable"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-). Available for read operations on the [`primary`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-states.md#mongodb-replstate-replstate.PRIMARY) only.; [`"snapshot"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-snapshot-). Available for [multi-document transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) and certain read operations outside of multi-document transactions. For more formation on the read concern levels, see [Read Concern Levels.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern-levels) The [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command uses the `readConcern` level specified in the originating `find` command. | | `max` | document | Optional. The *exclusive* upper bound for a specific index. See [`cursor.max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) for details. To use the `max` field, the command must also use `hint` unless the specified `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `min` | document | Optional. The *inclusive* lower bound for a specific index. See [`cursor.min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) for details. To use the `min` field, the command must also use `hint` unless the specified `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `returnKey` | boolean | Optional. If true, returns only the index keys in the resulting documents. Defaults to false. If returnKey is true and the [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) command does not use an index, the returned documents are empty. | | `showRecordId` | boolean | Optional. Determines whether to return the record identifier for each document. If true, adds a field $recordId to the returned documents. | | `tailable` | boolean | Optional. Returns a [tailable cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-tailable-cursor) for a capped collections. | | `awaitData` | boolean | Optional. Use with the tailable option to block a [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command on the cursor temporarily at the end of data rather than returning no data. After a timeout period, [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) returns as normal. | | `noCursorTimeout` | boolean | Optional. Prevents the server from timing out non-session idle cursors after an inactivity period of 30 minutes. Ignored for cursors that are part of a session. For more information, see [Session Idle Timeout.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-session-idle-timeout) | | [allowPartialResults](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-cmd-find-allowPartialResults) | boolean | Optional. For queries against a sharded collection, allows the command (or subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands) to return partial results instead of an error if one or more queried shards are unavailable. If [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) (or subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands) returns partial results because the queried shard(s) aren't available, the [find output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-cmd-find-output) includes a `partialResultsReturned` indicator field. If the queried shards are available for the initial `find` command, but one or more shards become unavailable for subsequent `getMore` commands, only the `getMore` commands that run while the shards aren't available include `partialResultsReturned` in their output. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-allowDiskUse) | boolean | Optional. Use this option to override [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) for a specific query. You can use this option to either: Prohibit disk use on a system where disk use is allowed by default.; Allow disk use on a system where disk use is prohibited by default. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, if [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) is set to `true` and the server requires more than 100 megabytes of memory for a pipeline execution stage, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies `{ allowDiskUse: false }`. For details, see [`allowDiskUseByDefault`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) `allowDiskUse` has no effect if MongoDB can satisfy the specified [sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-sort) using an index, *or* if the in-memory sort requires less than 100 megabytes of memory. For more complete documentation on `allowDiskUse`, see [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) For more information on memory restrictions for large in-memory sorts, see [Sort and Index Use.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-index-use) | | [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-let-syntax) | document | Optional. Specifies a document with a list of variables. This allows you to improve command readability by separating the variables from the query text. The document syntax is: `{ <variable_name_1>: <expression_1>, ..., <variable_name_n>: <expression_n> }` The variable is set to the value returned by the expression, and cannot be changed afterwards. To access the value of a variable in the command, use the double dollar sign prefix (`$$`) together with your variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example: `$$targetTotal`. To use a variable to filter results, you must access the variable within the [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) operator. For a complete example using `let` and variables, see [Use Variables in `let`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-let-example) **New in version 5.0** | | `querySettings` | document | Optional. Query settings that apply only to this execution of the command. The `querySettings` document accepts the following fields: `indexHints`; `queryFramework`; `reject`; `comment`; `queryKnobs`; `maxTimeMS` For descriptions of these fields, see [Command Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-fields) MongoDB doesn't store these settings on the cluster, and they don't apply to other queries with the same [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). To set query settings that persist for a query shape, use [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) MongoDB combines the settings that you pass in the command with any query settings stored on the cluster for the same query shape. If both settings specify the same field, the stored cluster setting takes precedence. **New in version 9.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#command-fields · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, index, projection, query operator anti-pattern, query shape

- [statement] A rooted $or (single top-level $or) with a sort may choose a blocking SORT over a faster SORT_MERGE because the subplanner picks the locally best plan per clause without considering sort order. A SORT stage instead of SORT_MERGE in explain('queryPlanner') diagnoses it. Ticket SERVER-19114 is Backlog/Unresolved, last updated 2025-03-26. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-19114 · keywords: $in, blocking sort, index, query operator anti-pattern, $in and $or Index Bounds and Union Plans

- [passage] Range queries can use [indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) to avoid scanning unwanted documents, typically yielding better performance as the offset grows compared to using [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) for pagination. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#using-range-queries · keywords: cursor, index, pagination, skip()
- [fact] When a sort is followed by a limit and no index supplies the order, the server keeps only the top k rows (about skip+limit) in sorter memory rather than all matches. It still examines every matching document, so an index-provided order remains the strongest option. — https://codemia.io/knowledge-hub/path/how_does_top-k_sort_algorithm_work_in_mongodb · keywords: blocking sort, index, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [passage] The following example uses the `key` option to specify that the aggregation should use the `location` field values for the `$geoNear` operation rather than the `legacy` field values. The pipeline also uses [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit) to return at most 5 documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.md#specify-which-geospatial-index-to-use · keywords: index, pagination, key, location, $geoNear, legacy
- [fact] The 10,000-document rule of thumb for preferring keyset over skip is a practitioner heuristic, not a measured benchmark; OpenReplay gives no timings. The only quantified offset-vs-seek numbers found are from Postgres (LIMIT 100 ~0.06 ms vs OFFSET 5,000,000 ~758 ms), which show the shape of the effect but not MongoDB's magnitude. — https://blog.openreplay.com/pagination-patterns-mongodb/ · keywords: pagination, Pagination Patterns (skip-limit vs range-keyset)
- [passage] - [`QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/error-codes.md#mongodb-error-292) when a stage that can spill to disk exceeds the limit and `allowDiskUse` is `false`. Run the operation with `{ allowDiskUse: true }` so that the stage spills to disk instead of failing. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#per-operation-memory-limit · keywords: blocking sort, QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed, allowDiskUse, false, { allowDiskUse: true } · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] If you run this example, the order of documents in your results might differ from the order of documents on this page because the aggregation pipeline does not contain a sort stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/aggregation-examples/unpack-arrays.md#steps · keywords: blocking sort

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Mitigations named by the Netdata guide: put the shard key or leading prefix in predicates, set maxTimeMS on unavoidable scatter-gather queries, avoid deep skip() pagination, and re-evaluate the shard key against dominant query shapes. A low-cardinality key (e.g. continent, at most seven chunks) limits scaling regardless of shard count. Single-vendor-blog advice; not independently verified. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-scatter-gather-queries/ · keywords: count, cursor, pagination, query shape, sharded query targeting, Sharded Query Targeting and Scatter-Gather
- [passage] | Metric | Description | | --- | --- | | Execution Count | Number of queries executed per hour which would be improved. | | Average Execution Time | Current average execution time in milliseconds for affected queries. | | Average Query Targeting | Average number of documents read per document returned by affected queries. A higher query targeting score indicates a greater degree of inefficiency. For more information on query targeting, see [Query Targeting.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#std-label-query-targeting) | | In Memory Sort | Current number of affected queries per hour that needed to be sorted in memory. | | Average Docs Scanned | Average number of documents scanned. | | Average Docs Returned | Average number of documents returned. | | Average Object Size | Average object size. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#index-metrics · keywords: blocking sort, count, index
- [statement] Workarounds for the rooted-$or SORT problem: hint one index that serves all clauses to force a merge sort; use an index filter (not persistent across restarts, set per node); or ensure each clause has an index providing the sort order and none offers an index requiring a blocking sort. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-19114 · keywords: $in, blocking sort, index, $in and $or Index Bounds and Union Plans
- [fact] Sorting on an indexed array field (multikey index) yields an in-memory SORT stage unless the index bounds for all sort fields are [MinKey, MaxKey] and no multikey field bounds share a path prefix with the sort pattern. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ · keywords: blocking sort, index, query operator anti-pattern, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [passage] If $in has fewer than 201 array elements, the elements are expanded and then merged in the sort order specified for the index using a SORT_MERGE stage. This improves performance for small arrays. In this case, $in is similar to an equality predicate with ESR. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: $in, blocking sort, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md
- [passage] cursor.allowDiskUse() has no effect on sort operations answered using an index or non-indexed ("in-memory") sort operations which require less than 100 megabytes of memory. For more complete documentation on in-memory sorts and sort index use, see Sort and Index Use. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/ · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, index
- [passage] See [Sort and Index Use](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-index-use) for more information on in-memory sort operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse.md#definition · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) has no effect on sort operations answered using an index *or* non-indexed ("in-memory") sort operations which require less than 100 megabytes of memory. For more complete documentation on in-memory sorts and sort index use, see [Sort and Index Use.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-index-use) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse.md#supports-large-non-indexed-sorts-only · keywords: blocking sort, cursor, index, cursor.allowDiskUse()
- [statement] SERVER-24027 (Core Server, fixed in 3.4.2/3.5.2, closed Jan 2017): for $or keyset pagination sorted descending on a compound key, the planner did not reverse an index scan to get SORT_MERGE and fell back to an in-memory sort. The pre-fix workaround was a descending index plus hint(). On pre-3.4.2 servers, check explain() for SORT or a blocking sort. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-24027 · keywords: blocking sort, index, pagination, Pagination Patterns (skip-limit vs range-keyset)

- [passage] The [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) method requires the server to scan from the beginning of the input results set before beginning to return results. As the offset increases, [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) will become slower. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#using-skip · keywords: cursor, pagination, skip()

- [passage] The following operation includes a [`cursor.sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) on the field `reading.timestamp`. - [fact] A compound index supports a sort on all its keys or on a prefix, with sort keys in index order. Directions must match the index pattern or its exact inverse: {a:1,b:-1} supports {a:1,b:-1} and {a:-1,b:1}, but not {a:1,b:1} or {a:-1,b:-1}. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ · keywords: blocking sort, index, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [fact] An index can serve a sort on a non-prefix subset of its keys only if the query has equality conditions on all index keys that precede the sort keys. With index {a,b,c,d}, find({a:{$gt:2}}).sort({c:1}) does not use the index efficiently. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ · keywords: blocking sort, index, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [fact] ESR guideline: put equality keys first, then sort keys, then range keys, so the index delivers sorted output without an in-memory sort. Sorting after equality also makes the sort non-blocking. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/ · keywords: blocking sort, index, Blocking Sort and Index-Backed Sort
- [passage] Call the [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) method on a cursor to control where MongoDB begins returning results. This approach may be useful in implementing paginated results. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#definition · keywords: cursor, pagination, skip()
- [passage] You must apply [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) to the cursor before retrieving any documents from the database. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#definition · keywords: cursor, pagination, skip()
- [passage] The [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) method has the following parameter: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#definition · keywords: cursor, pagination, skip()
- [passage] The [`skip()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#mongodb-method-cursor.skip) method controls the starting point of the results set. The following operation skips the first `5` documents in the [bios collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bios-example-collection.md#std-label-bios-example-collection) and returns all remaining documents: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#set-the-starting-point-of-the-result-set · keywords: cursor, pagination, skip()
- [passage] - Choose a field such as `_id` which generally changes in a consistent direction over time and has a [unique index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique) to prevent duplicate values, — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.skip.md#descending-order · keywords: index, pagination, _id
- [passage] Sort operations that use an index often have better performance than in-memory sorts. - [passage] "Sort" determines the order for results. - [passage] See Sort and Index Use for more information on in-memory sort operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/ · keywords: blocking sort, index
- [fact] MongoDB's documented range-query pagination: pick a field such as _id that changes consistently over time and has a unique index, filter with $lt (descending) or $gt (ascending), sort on it, and store the last-seen value for the next query. Range queries use indexes to avoid scanning unwanted documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.2/reference/method/cursor.skip/ · keywords: index, pagination, Pagination Patterns (skip-limit vs range-keyset)
- [fact] For a non-unique sort field such as createdAt, keyset pagination needs a compound filter: $or of {createdAt < last} and {createdAt == last, _id < lastId}, sorted by {createdAt:-1,_id:-1}, backed by an index with the same fields and directions. — https://blog.openreplay.com/pagination-patterns-mongodb/ · keywords: index, pagination, Pagination Patterns (skip-limit vs range-keyset)
